subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage for Dedicated + VPC/private deployment
messages:
From: Jake Morrison <jake@acmeanalytics.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: alan.miller@thirdshore-audit.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 report scope question for our Dedicated instance

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is going through vendor onboarding and they want to confirm two things before we proceed:

1) Does Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and any bridge letter explicitly cover Dedicated (reserved capacity) deployments that are isolated for a single customer, or is it limited to multi-tenant hosted API environments?

2) For customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), what artifacts/evidence do you provide to demonstrate control coverage (network isolation diagrams, logging/retention evidence, and any SOC2-specific scope statements)?

Our auditor (Alan Miller, cc'd) may follow up with specific evidence requests. Can you confirm what you can share and whether we need a custom bridge letter or an attestation for our Dedicated pool?

Appreciate a quick summary and any approximate timeline — our procurement approval is timeboxed to the end of this month.

Best,
Jake Morrison\Security Operations\Acme Analytics

---

(attachment: ACME_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx referenced)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Jake Morrison <jake@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Alan Miller <alan.miller@thirdshore-audit.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report scope question for our Dedicated instance

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:

1) Our SOC 2 Type II report (attached) covers the Redwood control environment for the covered period and applies to our hosted API and Dedicated (reserved capacity) offering when the customer uses Redwood-managed dedicated pools. For single-tenant Dedicated pools that run in our tenant-isolated infrastructure, the report can be considered in-scope for controls that are implemented and operated by Redwood (e.g., infrastructure hardening, access controls, logging, change management).

2) For Private (VPC / customer-managed) deployments, the standard SOC 2 report does not directly attest controls operated by the customer. In those cases we provide:
  - A bridge letter that documents which control responsibilities remain with the customer vs Redwood (attached template).
  - Evidence packages for controls we still operate (e.g., deployment packaging, update processes, KMS integration guidance).
  - Network isolation diagrams and sample logging extracts on request.

I've attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted), SOC2-bridge-letter-template.docx, and a sample network-isolation-diagram.png stub.

Alan — looping you in since you were cc'd; if ThirdShore needs to request specific evidence artifacts (log samples, change-control tickets), we can assemble them on a short timeline.

Jake — key caveats:
- Dedicated pools that are Redwood-managed and hosted in our environment are typically included in the report scope (we define the population in the report).
- For Dedicated where the customer brings their own infrastructure or for fully customer-hosted Private installs, the bridge letter will enumerate shared/residual responsibilities.
- Audit period: our current Type II covers 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30; if your audit window falls outside that, we can provide a bridge letter and as-needed evidence to cover interim periods.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jake — confirm whether your Dedicated instance will be Redwood-managed or customer-hosted.
2) If customer-hosted, share the evidence checklist from your auditor and we'll map responsibilities and produce a bridge letter.
3) Alan — if you need specific evidence artifacts, let us know the formats and acceptable redaction.

Thanks,

Aditya Rao\Senior Solutions Engineer\Redwood Inference\aditya_rao@redwood.ai
(attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf, SOC2-bridge-letter-template.docx, network-isolation-diagram.png)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Jake Morrison <jake@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report scope question for our Dedicated instance

Thanks Aditya — adding a few procurement/contract notes from our side:

- Pricing/terms: if Acme requires Redwood to take responsibility for controls in their Dedicated pool beyond our standard managed scope (e.g., additional logging retention, custom archive), that may require a small SOW. We should flag that early.
- Evidence turnaround: simple artifacts (redacted log extracts, control narratives) — 3 business days. Deeper evidence (ticket-level change history, long-term archives) — 7-10 business days.
- Bridge letter: we can customize for Acme; legal prefers to use our template with customer-specific insertions only.

Aditya/Neha: please confirm the artifact list we can commit to assembling if Acme requests the following:
  * Network isolation diagram (Redwood-managed layout)
  * Redacted access logs for the last 90 days (system-level events)
  * Change control summary for code releases impacting Dedicated pools during the SOC period
  * KMS integration checklist and evidence of key rotation policy enforcement

Jake — if you can confirm whether your Dedicated is Redwood-managed and which of the above you want, we’ll turn around a bridge + evidence package and include a short note about the SOC period coverage.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop\Director, Customer Success (Enterprise)\Redwood Inference\lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Alan Miller <alan.miller@thirdshore-audit.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report scope question for our Dedicated instance

Thanks — quick clarifying notes from ThirdShore:

- For our purposes, evidence that a Redwood-managed Dedicated pool is included in the SOC 2 population is sufficient (we will accept the SOC report + a signed bridge letter stating that Redwood operates the control for that Dedicated pool).
- For customer-hosted or VPC patterns, we will expect a bridge letter plus sampled artifacts for the controls Redwood still maintains.
- Preferred formats: PDF for reports, CSV/TSV for log extracts (sample), PNG/PDF for diagrams. Redaction is acceptable for PII.

Aditya/Redwood team — please provide the SOC2 PDF and a proposed bridge letter template by COB Wed 26 Aug if possible. If you can indicate the expected turnaround for any additional artifacts, include that in your response.

Regards,
Alan Miller\Senior Manager – Information Assurance\ThirdShore Audit & Advisory
